name: security-oauth-device-authorization-review
intent: Device Authorization Grant account/device transaction binding
artifacts: Device/user-code issuance, verification UI, polling client identity, expiry and owned test accounts/devices.
trace: Separate the device transaction, user confirmation and polling client. Determine which account and audience the final token represents, including user-visible confirmation.
experiment: In an owned issuer fixture confirm one device transaction, then compare another client/device transaction and expired/reused codes without guessing user codes.
disproof: A deliberately portable user code is not a flaw by itself; no token issuance or wrong-account binding means the strong claim is unproved.
repair: Bind the approved transaction, client and account; retest legitimate pairing, expiry and unauthorized transaction substitution.
branch_decisions: Distinguish device_code, human user_code and the polling client; they have different audiences. A user confirmation must be tied to the intended device transaction, but cross-device confirmation is normal. Use expiry/polling errors as protocol observations, not evidence of account authentication unless a token is actually issued.
operational_method: Identify issuer, client_id, device_code and the approved user transaction in the polling state. Public clients are identified differently from confidential clients that authenticate. Separate authorization_pending, access_denied and expired_token states from successful token issuance; a user_code displayed on another device is normal. Compare rightful polling with a client/transaction mismatch in an owned issuer fixture, without asking a real user to approve an attacker transaction.
